response.title: Can I mount regular solar panels on my van roof and plug them into a power station instead of buying the brand's folding panels?
response.answer:
Yes! You can absolutely mount regular residential-style solar panels on your van roof and connect them directly to a portable power station, instead of buying the power station manufacturer's expensive folding solar panels.

In fact, for a van with a permanent solar installation, this is often a better and more cost-effective solution.

Most portable power stations from brands like EcoFlow, Bluetti, Jackery, and Anker can accept third-party solar panels, provided the electrical specifications are compatible.

1. How the setup works
Shop

Rigid solar panels on van roof

Solar cables (MC4 connectors)

Through a weatherproof roof cable entry

Adapter to power station solar input

Often XT60, XT60i, Anderson, or DC7909

Portable power station

Built-in MPPT solar charge controller

You generally don't need a separate solar charge controller, because most modern power stations already have an MPPT controller built in.

2. The most important thing: voltage compatibility

Before buying panels, check these four specifications:

Specification

	

What to check




Voltage (Voc)

	

Must stay below the station's maximum solar input voltage, including in cold weather




Operating voltage (Vmp)

	

Must be within the station's MPPT operating range




Current (Isc/Imp)

	

Must comply with the station's input limits




Wattage (W)

	

Determines potential charging speed, subject to the station's maximum input

For example, the EcoFlow DELTA 2 supports 500W of solar input, with a 60V maximum and 15A input limit. A compatible 400W rigid panel could work, but some residential 400W panels have voltages or currents that make them unsuitable. 
EcoFlow Manuals

Connecting multiple panels also matters: series wiring increases voltage, while parallel wiring increases current. 
EcoFlow Manuals

3. Rigid vs. folding solar panels

Usually lower

Permanent mounting

	

Excellent

Durability

	

Often excellent

	

Depends on design




Portability

	

Poor

	

Excellent




Charging while driving

	

Yes

Position toward sunlight

	

Fixed

	

Adjustable




Weight

	

Typically heavier

	

Often lighter

For a van, I'd generally choose rigid panels with aluminum frames, securely attached to a roof rack or engineered mounting brackets.

Make sure the roof can support the weight and aerodynamic loads, allow ventilation underneath, protect cables from abrasion, and use weatherproof cable entries. Residential panels can be quite large, so measure your roof before buying.

4. One more consideration

If you're planning to keep your power station inside the van, you can make the system semi-permanent: leave the solar panels mounted and simply unplug the power station whenever you want to take it elsewhere.

Just keep the power station within its specified operating temperature range, especially when the van is parked in the sun.

5. I can help you find the right panels

Two questions:

Which power station do you have (or plan to buy)? For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, Bluetti AC200L, Anker SOLIX C1000, etc.

What van do you have? For example, Ford Transit, Mercedes Sprinter, Ram ProMaster, or a minivan.

With those two details, I can help you figure out how many watts of regular solar panels will fit on your roof, how to connect them safely, and whether you can save money compared with the branded folding panels.
